ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a large rectangle, divided into 7 squares. On the right side is a column of 3 gray squares, stacked up and down, and the problem gives that the side length of each gray square is 8 cm. In the upper left is a black square, and in the lower left, below the black square, there are 3 white squares placed side by side. Reasoning: The 3 gray squares on the right are stacked vertically, so the height of the whole large rectangle is 3×8=24 cm. Let the side length of each bottom white square be x cm, and the side length of the black square be b cm. From the figure it can be seen that the width of the black square is exactly equal to the total width of the 3 white squares below, so b=3x. The height of the left side of the large rectangle is composed of the black square and one white square vertically, so b+x=24. Substituting b=3x, we get 3x+x=24, namely 4x=24, x=6. Therefore b=3×6=18 cm.
